# Rules

wormsign has 46 rules. Each finding carries one rule ID. This page is generated from the rule catalogue
in `src/rules.ts`, which is also where the SARIF output takes each rule's description and help text, and every
SARIF rule's `helpUri` points at the rule's section here. `test/docs-rules.test.ts` fails when this page is out of
date.

Severity is set per finding, not per rule: the same rule can report different severities in different
situations, listed under each rule. "Set by the IOC entry" means the severity comes from the matching entry in the
IOC data (`data/iocs/`, see [iocs.md](iocs.md)). How severities map to exit codes and to GitHub code scanning is in
[output.md](output.md); how to suppress a reviewed finding is in [baseline.md](baseline.md).

## Lifecycle scripts in package.json (WS-LC)

### WS-LC-001

**install-lifecycle-script**

package.json defines a preinstall/install/postinstall script, which runs automatically when the package is installed. Also reported for a .gyp file beside a package.json when a package manager runs node-gyp rebuild on it at install, and gyp runs the shell commands in \<!(...) expansions: npm for any .gyp file with no install or preinstall script and gypfile not false, pnpm for binding.gyp with no install or preinstall script, and Yarn 1 for binding.gyp with no install script. pnpm and Yarn 1 ignore gypfile, and an empty script counts as none.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md)
- **Severity:** low, medium. Low when package.json has "private": true (the script runs only for installs of this project); medium otherwise, because the script runs for everyone who installs the package.
- **What to do:** Confirm the script is needed and review exactly what it runs. Installing with --ignore-scripts (or ignore-scripts=true in .npmrc) stops lifecycle scripts from running.

### WS-LC-002

**suspicious-lifecycle-script**

A lifecycle script matches a download-and-execute, encoded-payload, or credential-harvesting pattern.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** high. Scan checks the project's manifests and, with --node-modules, installed packages; diff checks install-time scripts the change adds or changes.
- **What to do:** Treat this as a likely compromise until reviewed: read the whole script, do not install this tree, and compare the package with its last known-good version.

### WS-LC-003

**ioc-lifecycle-script**

A lifecycle script references a payload filename from the sourced IOC list.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** high, critical. Critical when the IOC list rates the payload file name high or critical on its own; high otherwise.
- **What to do:** Treat this as a compromise: do not install, remove or replace the package, and rotate the credentials (npm, GitHub, cloud) on every machine that ran the install.

### WS-LC-004

**package-manager-runs-repo-code**

The repository holds code a package manager runs without any lifecycle script: a .pnpmfile.cjs or .pnpmfile.mjs (pnpm runs its hooks on install), .env.yarn (Yarn 4 loads it into every script), a file under .yarn/releases or .yarn/plugins, a Plug'n'Play loader (.pnp.cjs, .pnp.loader.mjs), or a file that config names as code to run. Also reported for that config: .yarnrc.yml yarnPath, plugins or injectEnvironmentFiles; .yarnrc yarn-path; pnpm-workspace.yaml pnpmfile or globalPnpmfile; .npmrc node-options (unless it only sets a memory or stack limit or what Node.js prints), script-shell, pnpmfile or global-pnpmfile.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md)
- **Severity:** high. Not reported inside node\_modules or under the baseline's ignorePaths, except for a file that config outside them names. A .yarnrc.yml or pnpm-workspace.yaml with YAML outside the subset wormsign reads is reported as WS-SC-900 instead, and so is such a file reached through a symlink.
- **What to do:** Read the code, or what the setting runs, before running any package-manager command in this directory: a yarnPath release runs on every yarn command, before any install. If it is the project's own reviewed code (a committed Yarn release, a pnpmfile), baseline the finding: its fingerprint holds a hash of the file's content or of the settings' values, so a later change is reported again. wormsign diff reports any change to these files as WS-DF-005.

## Lockfile entries (WS-LK)

### WS-LK-001

**ioc-package-version**

A lockfile pins a package@version listed as compromised in the sourced IOC list.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** critical. Scan checks lockfiles and, with --node-modules, installed packages; diff checks the lockfile entries a change adds.
- **What to do:** Move to a version that is not on the IOC list, regenerate the lockfile, and rotate the credentials on every machine and CI runner that installed the compromised version.

### WS-LK-002

**non-registry-resolution**

A lockfile entry resolves from somewhere other than an allowed npm registry host.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** medium, high. Medium for a git source; high for another host, plain HTTP, a value that is not a registry URL, a registry URL that names another package, or a runtime binary downloaded from somewhere other than its official release site.
- **What to do:** Check that this source is expected. If the package should come from the registry, reinstall it from there; if the host is a trusted private registry, allow it with --registry-host.

### WS-LK-003

**missing-integrity**

A registry-resolved lockfile entry has no integrity hash, so tampering with the tarball would go unnoticed.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** medium. Not reported for Yarn Berry lockfiles, which record a checksum of Yarn's own archive format rather than a registry integrity, or for bundled dependencies. A Yarn 1 entry with no integrity line is not reported when its resolved URL ends in # and a 40-hex SHA-1, which Yarn 1 verifies; that SHA-1 is its integrity.
- **What to do:** Regenerate the lockfile with a current package manager so that every registry entry records an integrity hash.

## GitHub Actions workflows (WS-GH)

### WS-GH-001

**ioc-workflow-file**

A workflow file has a name from the sourced IOC list.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** set by the IOC entry. The severity of the matching entry in data/iocs/workflows.json.
- **What to do:** Delete the workflow, treat the repository as compromised, and rotate every secret the workflow could read.

### WS-GH-002

**secrets-dump**

A workflow expression reads the whole secrets context: toJSON(secrets), the object filter secrets.\* (as in toJSON(secrets.\*) or join(secrets.\*, ' ')), secrets passed to any function such as format, or a secrets\[...\] index computed at run time; in short, any use of secrets other than secrets.NAME or secrets\['NAME'\]. Context and function names match in any case, as GitHub reads them.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** high
- **What to do:** Pass each step only the secrets it needs, as individual environment variables (secrets.NAME). toJSON(secrets), secrets.\* and a computed secrets\[...\] index hand every secret available to the workflow to that step.

### WS-GH-003

**pull-request-target-head-checkout**

A pull\_request\_target or workflow\_run workflow checks out code from the pull request: its head ref in a ref: value or a git fetch or checkout, written out or through an env: variable bound to it, or a ref: computed from the github context (toJSON, fromJSON or a computed index), which wormsign cannot resolve. Not followed, so not reported: a head ref passed through a step output, a file or $GITHUB\_ENV.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** high
- **What to do:** Do not run pull request code in a pull\_request\_target or workflow\_run workflow, which can read secrets and get a write token. Use the pull\_request trigger for untrusted code.

### WS-GH-004

**self-hosted-runner**

A workflow runs on a self-hosted runner.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** medium
- **What to do:** Use self-hosted runners only for trusted repositories, and prefer ephemeral runners so that a compromised job cannot persist on the machine.

### WS-GH-005

**secret-to-file-or-network**

A workflow step passes a secret, directly or through an env: variable, to a command that writes a file or uses the network. Not followed, so not reported: a secret the script assigns to a shell variable and uses on a later line (T="${{ secrets.TOKEN }}", then curl -d "$T"), or passes through a file, an action input or a step output.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** high
- **What to do:** Give the secret only to the tool that needs it, through an environment variable, and do not write it to disk or send it to other hosts.

### WS-GH-006

**ioc-runner-name**

A workflow targets a runner name or label from the sourced IOC list.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** critical
- **What to do:** Take the runner and its host out of service, investigate the host as compromised, and rotate every credential it could reach.

### WS-GH-007

**discussion-trigger-with-run**

A workflow is triggered by discussion events and runs shell commands (used as a remote-command backdoor by a reported variant).

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** medium, high. High when a job in the workflow runs on a self-hosted runner (the shape of the reported backdoor); medium otherwise.
- **What to do:** Remove the discussion trigger or the run steps. Discussion events can come from users without write access and should not drive shell commands.

## Payload files (WS-FS)

### WS-FS-001

**ioc-payload-hash**

A file's SHA-256 matches a payload hash from the sourced IOC list.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md)
- **Severity:** critical
- **What to do:** Treat this as a compromise: delete the file and rotate the credentials (npm, GitHub, cloud) on every machine where it ran.

### WS-FS-002

**payload-filename**

A file has a name associated with worm payloads in the sourced IOC list.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md)
- **Severity:** set by the IOC entry. The nameOnlySeverity of the matching entry in data/iocs/files.json. Names rated info are not reported. A file whose hash matches is reported as WS-FS-001 instead.
- **What to do:** Inspect the file. A name match is weaker evidence than a hash match; if the file is not expected, treat it as a compromise.

## Exfiltration endpoints (WS-EX)

### WS-EX-001

**exfil-endpoint**

A file contains a hardcoded webhook, paste, or request-capture endpoint.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md)
- **Severity:** medium. Not checked inside node\_modules, where these hosts are common.
- **What to do:** Confirm that the endpoint is expected. Code that sends data to webhook, paste or request-capture services is a common exfiltration channel.

### WS-EX-002

**ioc-exfil-endpoint**

A file contains an exfiltration endpoint from the sourced IOC list.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md)
- **Severity:** set by the IOC entry. The severity of the matching entry in data/iocs/endpoints.json.
- **What to do:** Treat this as a compromise: remove the code and rotate every credential it could have read.

## Installed packages (node_modules) (WS-NM)

### WS-NM-001

**installed-package-install-script**

An installed package in node\_modules declares an install-time script.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md)
- **Severity:** low, medium. Only with --node-modules. Medium for a preinstall, install or postinstall script; low for a binding.gyp without one, for which npm runs node-gyp rebuild.
- **What to do:** Review the package's install script. Installing with --ignore-scripts stops install scripts from running.

## Editor and AI-agent persistence (WS-PS)

### WS-PS-001

**editor-auto-run-task**

A VS Code task runs automatically (runOptions.runOn folderOpen or worktreeCreated) from .vscode/tasks.json, the tasks section of .vscode/settings.json, or a \*.code-workspace file, so opening the folder runs its command and those of the tasks it depends on; or a settings file sets what tasks run with (a tasks section, or the terminal profile and environment settings tasks use). Always high, whatever the command; the message adds reasons when the command matches the lifecycle-script heuristics or an IOC file name.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** high. Whatever the command it runs.
- **What to do:** High whatever it runs: each automatic task in .vscode/tasks.json or a \*.code-workspace file; each top-level dotted key there (VS Code reads "linux.tasks" as nested task settings); and, in .vscode/settings.json or a workspace's settings, one entry for any tasks section (nested or dotted tasks.\* keys) and one for the terminal settings tasks run with (terminal.integrated.automationProfile, defaultProfile, profiles, env). Remove runOn unless needed, or review and baseline it. A task's fingerprint covers it, the tasks its dependsOn reaches and its file's global settings (the whole file for a dotted key or an unresolved or over-long dependsOn); a settings entry's covers all it lists. A script a task runs (or an npm task's script), a setting it reads with ${config:...} and settings outside the repository can change without a new finding. VS Code runs automatic tasks only in a trusted workspace; while task.allowAutomaticTasks is unset it asks once per workspace, and Allow turns them on for every trusted workspace.

### WS-PS-002

**agent-settings-command**

A Claude Code settings file, plugin file, skill/command/subagent frontmatter or project .mcp.json makes Claude Code run something automatically: a hook of any event or type, a command setting such as statusLine or apiKeyHelper, an env entry outside a few inert settings, or an MCP server that runs a local command or a headersHelper. Always high, whatever the command; the message adds reasons when it matches the lifecycle-script heuristics or an IOC file name.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** high. Whatever the command it runs.
- **What to do:** High whatever it runs: every settings-file hook, command setting such as statusLine, project MCP server that runs a local command or a headersHelper, env entry other than a few inert model, limit and telemetry settings, plugin or marketplace a settings file adds, plugin file under .claude/, and skill, command or subagent file under .claude/ whose frontmatter mentions hooks or mcpServers or holds a backslash (wormsign does not parse YAML, so a mere mention counts). A symlink under .claude/ is WS-SC-900. Not reported: a skill's !\`command\` lines and allowed-tools, a plugin's other files, a plugin outside .claude/. Review each entry and any script it runs, then baseline it: the fingerprint covers the entry, so editing it reports it again, but the script can change unseen. claude -p and SDK sessions run most of these at once, an interactive session once you trust the folder. To keep hooks from running in a repository you have not reviewed, start Claude Code with --bare or --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'.

## Scan coverage (WS-SC)

### WS-SC-900

**file-not-checked**

A file that decides what runs at install time or in CI (manifest, lockfile, workflow, or code or config a package manager runs, see WS-LC-004) could not be checked: unreadable, too large, binary, invalid, a symlink (to a file or package directory), or an unsupported format; a workflow in YAML the reader does not model (flow or JSON form, flow jobs or steps, aliases, merge keys, the line breaks U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029), or with a ${{ }} expression it cannot read (one outside a comment with no closing }} within 50 lines, or one written in part with YAML escapes); two such files whose paths differ only in case, Unicode form or trailing periods and spaces, of which a case-insensitive disk or Windows holds only one; a code file that could not be searched for exfiltration endpoints from the IOC list; or a workspaces pattern (package.json workspaces, pnpm-workspace.yaml packages) that can match a package the scan does not read (under an ignored path, node\_modules or .git, or outside the repository).

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md)
- **Severity:** low, high. High by default; low for a symlink to a directory that holds no package.json and that wormsign does not scan, and for a code file that could not be searched for exfiltration endpoints from the IOC list (unreadable, or larger than 64 MiB).
- **What to do:** Make the file readable by wormsign or review it by hand. The finding is high by default because the package manager or GitHub may still act on the file.

## Pull request diff (WS-DF)

### WS-DF-001

**new-dependency-install-script**

A pull request adds a dependency that runs install-time scripts, including a local package (a workspace or file: directory) that an npm lockfile records with install scripts.

- **Reported by:** [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** high
- **What to do:** Review the new dependency and its install script before merging. Install scripts run on every machine and CI runner that installs the project. A reviewed one gets through today in one of two ways: the owner of the required check overrides it for this pull request, or a pull request that baselines the finding lands first, which itself fails WS-DF-005 and needs the same override. A narrower route, an opt-in code-owner approval of the baseline change, is accepted but not yet built (docs/adr/0008-baseline-approval-route.md).

### WS-DF-002

**lifecycle-script-changed**

A pull request adds or changes a lifecycle script that an install runs, or a .gyp file beside a package.json, for which npm, pnpm or Yarn 1 can run node-gyp rebuild. Also reported for an unchanged .gyp file when the change adds the package.json beside it, or removes or empties its install script, preinstall script or gypfile: false, so that npm, pnpm or Yarn 1 starts running node-gyp on it. pnpm and Yarn 1 run binding.gyp even with gypfile: false, so a package.json added with gypfile: false is reported too.

- **Reported by:** [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** medium. A suspicious or IOC script is also reported as WS-LC-002 or WS-LC-003.
- **What to do:** Review the lifecycle script change before merging. It runs automatically on install.

### WS-DF-003

**workflow-changed**

A pull request adds or changes a GitHub Actions workflow.

- **Reported by:** [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** medium. Covers workflows and local actions (action.yml, action.yaml); the workflow rules WS-GH-\* also run on the new content.
- **What to do:** Review the workflow change before merging. Workflows on the default branch can read repository secrets.

### WS-DF-004

**dependency-install-script-added**

A pull request changes a dependency's version to one that now has install scripts.

- **Reported by:** [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** high
- **What to do:** Review the new version's install script before merging and compare the version with the previous one.

### WS-DF-005

**install-policy-changed**

A pull request adds, changes or removes what controls installs or what wormsign reports: package-manager config (.npmrc, .yarnrc, .yarnrc.yml, pnpm-workspace.yaml, .pnpmfile.cjs, bunfig.toml, pip.conf, pip.ini, uv.toml, a pyproject.toml's \[tool.uv\] install settings), code that config runs, the build of a Python project no uv.lock or pylock.toml lists (what decides its build requirements, which an install that builds it resolves fresh: \[build-system\], setup.cfg, setup.py, hatch.toml, hook files), the packageManager field, the workspaces field, a dependency spec that installs from a local path, or the wormsign baseline; or it removes a lockfile (npm's, a Python lock, or a requirements file holding hashes), or strips a requirements file of its hashes (one found by name, or by its --hash options as soak finds one: deps.txt, deps.lock.in).

- **Reported by:** [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** high
- **What to do:** Review the change to the policy file itself. A change that weakens a release-age setting, re-enables install scripts or adds a baseline entry can silence the other checks for this pull request.

### WS-DF-006

**changed-file-not-checked**

A pull request changes a manifest or lockfile that wormsign could not read or parse, or a bun lockfile, which wormsign does not parse, so nothing in it was checked. Also reported on every run for a .yarnrc.yml or pnpm-workspace.yaml with anything outside the YAML subset wormsign reads, since the code it names could not be followed. A changed Python lockfile or requirements file, and any change to a pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg or Pipfile, is reported at medium: diff does not check what they pin or declare, and soak --base checks the locks.

- **Reported by:** [`diff`](cli/diff.md)
- **Severity:** medium, high. Medium for a changed Python lockfile or requirements file, and for any change to a pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg or Pipfile (the file compared whole), which diff does not resolve and soak --base checks the locks of; not what a manifest names (a hook, a dependency file). High otherwise (a pyproject.toml that cannot be parsed included).
- **What to do:** Fix the file so it parses, or review its changes by hand. The finding fails closed because the package manager may still act on the file. For a Python lockfile, requirements file or manifest, run \`wormsign soak --base \<base\>\` on the change, which checks what the locks pin.

## Soak time (WS-SK)

### WS-SK-001

**package-too-new**

A locked package version was published less than the required soak time ago.

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** high
- **What to do:** Pin the previous version, or wait until this version has been published for the required soak time. In PR mode (--base) an npm or Python entry the base's own soak read identically (the same lock file, name, version and hashes) is not checked again, so a young version pushed directly to the base passes later pull requests: the full soak on push and on a schedule catches it. A pin that lands first in a file the base's soak never read as a lock is checked once a change makes it one.

### WS-SK-002

**soak-unverifiable**

The publish time or identity of a locked package version could not be verified; treated as failing (fail closed). npm, pnpm, Yarn and bun: a missing, unreadable or unsupported lockfile, a git or off-registry source, a private registry, a version not on the registry, an integrity that differs from the registry's, or a registry error. PyPI: a lockfile soak does not read yet (poetry.lock, pdm.lock, Pipfile.lock), a manifest or PEP 723 script that no lock covers, a requirements file that is not a complete --require-hashes lock, a locked file without a sha256 or that is not a file of that project and version on the index (deleted, quarantined or never published), a git, URL or other-index source, a local source that is not in the reviewed tree, an install setting that may use another index or skip hash checks, or an index error.

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** medium, high. Medium only for a local Python project whose one problem is files git does not track, on a run without --base (a developer's checkout); with --base that is high too.
- **What to do:** Fix what the finding names (commit the lockfile, install from the registry, or make the registry reachable with --registry or --pypi-index) and run the check again. For Python, lock with uv (uv lock), or write a hash lock (uv pip compile --generate-hashes, with --require-hashes in the file), and install with --locked, --frozen or --require-hashes. The gate fails closed when it cannot verify a package. Of the requirements-file problems, a baseline can approve only a plain index requirement soak parsed to the end and a local file it resolved to a regular file inside the repository; any other (an option, an include, a path soak cannot pin, a line it could not read, a halt, the missing --require-hashes line) is never suppressed: fix the line as its message says.

### WS-SK-003

**soak-config-missing**

No package-manager release-age setting enforcing the soak time was found in project configuration.

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** low, medium, high. Low for Yarn Classic, which has no release-age setting; medium otherwise; --require-config raises medium to high.
- **What to do:** Add the release-age setting the finding names for this package manager. Where none exists (Yarn Classic), run \`wormsign soak\` in CI as the gate.

### WS-SK-004

**soak-config-too-short**

A package-manager release-age setting is shorter than required, cannot be interpreted, is ignored by the package-manager version that will run (or that version is unknown), or is bypassed by an exclusion or trust setting.

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** medium, high. Medium; --require-config raises it to high.
- **What to do:** Fix what the finding names: set the value to at least the required soak time, run a package-manager version that enforces it, or remove the setting that bypasses it. For Yarn, write plain minutes: Yarn 4.10 reads a unit suffix as minutes ("7d" is 7 minutes), while 4.11 and later accept suffixes.

### WS-SK-005

**install-time-resolution**

A Python install builds a package from source, and the build's requirements are resolved when it runs, outside every lockfile soak reads: a local project the install builds (a uv directory or editable member, a pylock directory entry), a package locked only as an sdist, or uv configuration in the tree that forces source builds (no-binary, no-build-isolation, extra-build-dependencies, config-settings). soak never locks, binds or ages build requirements.

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** medium, high. Python locks only. Medium on a full run, so the default --fail-on high reports it without failing: most Python projects build something. In PR mode (--base) a build the change adds is high; one the base has stays medium. --require-config does not raise it.
- **What to do:** Avoid the build where you can: \`uv sync --locked --no-install-project\` or \`\[tool.uv\] package = false\` for a project that need not be installed, a version with wheels for the platforms you install on, no build-forcing settings. Otherwise pin the build requirements with ==-pinned build constraints (uv build-constraint-dependencies, pip --build-constraint) and keep the installer's release-age cutoff, which is all that protects them. A reviewed local build can be baselined with a justification: its key changes when its build requirements or build files do. In PR mode (--base) a build the change adds is high, so the default --fail-on high stops it; one the base already had stays medium.

### WS-SK-006

**soak-outage-unverified**

Reported only with --on-outage warn: a locked package version was not checked because the npm registry or the Python index was out for the whole run. Its request failed after soak's retry in transport before any status line (a DNS or connection error, a TLS handshake that broke off, a timeout) or with HTTP 429 or a 5xx; the host gave no other answer in the run; and a HEAD probe of its root after the run got none either. Its age, identity and OSV records are unverified. Without the option the same package is WS-SK-002, high, and so it stays under the option when the host answered anything, including a host that went down mid-run, and for every other problem: HTTP 404 or another 4xx, a redirect, a body that is slow, cut off or does not parse, a certificate the client rejects, an integrity mismatch, a private registry or a name wormsign cannot vouch for.

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** medium. Only with --on-outage warn, when the npm registry or the Python index gave no answer in the whole run nor to the probe after it; never suppressed by a baseline.
- **What to do:** The trade-off: under --on-outage warn an outage of the whole configured host no longer fails the gate at the default --fail-on high, so whoever can make that host unreachable from the runner for the entire run (an outage, a firewall rule, an attacker on the network path) can merge a change whose packages were never checked, recorded only by this finding and the run's UNVERIFIED line. One name the registry will not serve is not enough: it stays WS-SK-002. Choose the option only where a gate that teams switch off is the worse risk, and run soak again once the host answers, before anything installs the change. A baseline never suppresses this finding: an outage is transient, and an entry for it would waive the next one.

## Registry signals (WS-RG)

### WS-RG-001

**registry-install-script-added**

A package version adds or changes a preinstall/install/postinstall script compared with the version it replaces, according to the registry's copy of its manifest.

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** high
- **What to do:** Read the new script before installing this version, and keep the previous version until you have. A reported worm adds a preinstall script to every package it republishes. False positives: a maintainer adding a native addon or a binary download. Not seen: a node-gyp build from a binding.gyp in the tarball, which the registry manifest does not show.

### WS-RG-002

**registry-provenance-dropped**

A package version was published without a provenance attestation, while the version it replaces had one.

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** high
- **What to do:** Find out how this version was published before installing it: npm creates provenance only in GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, so a stolen token used anywhere else publishes without it. False positives: a maintainer publishing by hand, or moving to a CI system that does not create provenance. Not seen: a worm publishing from the package's own release workflow, which gets valid provenance, or from CI of its own, whose provenance names another repository (check it with npm audit signatures and the attestation).

### WS-RG-003

**registry-new-publisher**

A package version was published, with a token or password, by an npm account that published none of the five versions before it.

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** medium
- **What to do:** Confirm with the project that this account is expected to publish. A worm publishes every package the stolen token can write, including ones its owner rarely releases. False positives: a maintainer handover or a new release manager. Publishes by a trusted publisher are not checked, since their provenance names the workflow that made them.

## OSV malicious-package records (WS-OS)

### WS-OS-001

**osv-malicious-package**

OSV has a malicious-package record for a locked package version: an OpenSSF malicious-packages record (id MAL-...), into which GitHub advisories of type malware are merged, or a GitHub advisory (id GHSA-...) whose CWE ids include CWE-506, embedded malicious code, which GitHub gives a hijacked release such as ua-parser-js@0.7.29. Both kinds are reported in every ecosystem that soak checks, one finding per record. Other records, such as ordinary vulnerabilities, are not reported.

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** critical. Not run with --no-osv.
- **What to do:** Treat this as a compromise: do not install this version, move the lockfile to a version without a record, and rotate the credentials (package registry, GitHub, cloud) on every machine and CI runner that installed it. The finding links to the record, which names the affected versions.

### WS-OS-900

**osv-not-checked**

Some locked package versions could not be checked against OSV (request failed, unexpected response, a GitHub advisory whose record could not be read, more than 1000 versions with GitHub advisories to read in one run, or not a registry name and version, such as a git dependency); treated as failing (fail closed).

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** high. Not run with --no-osv.
- **What to do:** Run the check again when api.osv.dev is reachable. When the message says more than 1000 versions had GitHub advisories to read, the versions past that limit (in name and version order, compared as plain strings, so 1.0.10 comes before 1.0.9) were not checked: run soak on fewer or smaller lockfiles, or run it with --no-osv and check the lockfiles with another OSV client. A dependency that is not a registry version cannot be looked up: review it by hand, and baseline the finding with a justification if it is trusted.

### WS-OS-901

**osv-outage-unchecked**

Reported only with --on-outage warn: a locked package version was not checked against OSV for malicious-package records because api.osv.dev was out for the whole run: its query batch failed after the retry in transport before any status line or with HTTP 429 or a 5xx, OSV gave no other answer in the run, and a HEAD probe of its root after the run got none either. One finding per version. Without the option these versions are in WS-OS-900, high, and so they stay under the option when OSV answered anything, for a record query that failed (it follows an answered batch), a redirect, HTTP 400 or another 4xx, an answer that does not parse or has the wrong shape, and every other reason.

- **Reported by:** [`soak`](cli/soak.md)
- **Severity:** medium. Only with --on-outage warn, when api.osv.dev gave no answer in the whole run nor to the probe after it; never suppressed by a baseline. Not run with --no-osv.
- **What to do:** The trade-off: under --on-outage warn an outage of api.osv.dev for the entire run no longer fails the gate at the default --fail-on high, so a version with a malware record can merge while OSV is unreachable from the runner, recorded only by this finding and the run's UNVERIFIED line. The soak time still applies. Run soak again once api.osv.dev answers, before anything installs the change. A baseline never suppresses this finding: an outage is transient, and an entry for it would waive the next one.

## GitHub organization audit (WS-OR)

### WS-OR-001

**org-ioc-repo**

A repository name or description matches a worm indicator pattern.

- **Reported by:** [`audit-org`](cli/audit-org.md)
- **Severity:** set by the IOC entry. The severity of the matching pattern in data/iocs/repos.json.
- **What to do:** Inspect the repository. If it was created by the worm, preserve evidence, make it private or delete it, and rotate the credentials it exposes.

### WS-OR-002

**org-visibility-flip**

Audit log shows a repository changed from private to public.

- **Reported by:** [`audit-org`](cli/audit-org.md)
- **Severity:** medium, high. Medium for each repository made public; one extra high finding when 3 or more were made public within 60 minutes.
- **What to do:** Confirm that the change was intended. If not, make the repository private again and find out who made the change.

### WS-OR-003

**org-runner**

A self-hosted runner registered on the organization or one of its repositories needs review.

- **Reported by:** [`audit-org`](cli/audit-org.md)
- **Severity:** low, critical. Critical when a runner's name matches a runner name in the IOC list; low for any other registered runner or runner registration event.
- **What to do:** Confirm that the runner is expected and that only trusted repositories can use it. Remove a runner with a worm IOC name and investigate its host.

### WS-OR-004

**org-ioc-workflow**

A repository contains a workflow file or branch whose name is in the sourced IOC list.

- **Reported by:** [`audit-org`](cli/audit-org.md)
- **Severity:** set by the IOC entry, high. For a workflow file, the severity of the matching entry in data/iocs/workflows.json; high for a branch named in data/iocs/repos.json.
- **What to do:** Delete the workflow file or branch, treat the repository as compromised, and rotate every secret the workflow could read.

### WS-OR-900

**org-audit-degraded**

Part of the organization audit could not run (GitHub plan or token scope, a rate limit, a GitHub or network error, or an answer that is not the documented one); coverage is reduced.

- **Reported by:** [`audit-org`](cli/audit-org.md)
- **Severity:** info. It does not fail the default gate; an audit that a rate limit stopped, whose per-repository checks no repository answered, or that left a repository or the organization runner inventory unchecked because of a GitHub or network error or an unexpected answer, exits 2 instead.
- **What to do:** For a scope gap, run the audit again with a token that has the access named in the finding; for a rate limit, a GitHub or network error or an unexpected answer, run it again later.

## Baseline (WS-BL)

### WS-BL-001

**baseline-entry-expired**

A baseline entry's expiry date has passed, so the finding is no longer suppressed.

- **Reported by:** [`scan`](cli/scan.md), [`diff`](cli/diff.md), [`soak`](cli/soak.md), [`audit-org`](cli/audit-org.md)
- **Severity:** medium. Reported by any command that applied a baseline with an expired entry.
- **What to do:** Fix the finding, or review it again and renew the baseline entry with a new expiry date.
